prompt: Clean up dead code in our monorepo before the refactor sprint.
context: Repo root: /work/platform with packages/api, packages/web, packages/shared. packages/shared is consumed by the other two.
rubric: Scans per package (cd packages/<name> && graph-it scan) rather than once at the monorepo root
Explains that a root-level scan produces cross-package false positives
Treats packages/shared exports as review-first because other packages consume them
Takes an architecture baseline (`graph-it architecture --format toon`) to identify entry points and generated areas first
anti_patterns: Runs one root scan and presents the result as authoritative
Marks shared-package exports as safe to delete
gold_notes: Monorepo rule: scan per package. Generated code and entry points need review, not automatic deletion.

prompt: We just ripped out the loyalty-points feature. Is anything left dangling?
context: Repo root: /work/shop. The feature's UI and routes were deleted in the previous commit; helper modules may remain.
rubric: Re-runs `graph-it scan` because imports changed in the previous commit
Runs the workspace-wide scan to find newly orphaned symbols and files
Proposes deletion in small, revertable commits with the test suite run between batches
anti_patterns: Uses a stale index without re-scanning after the removal commit
Bundles every deletion into one large commit
gold_notes: Re-scan after any refactor that changed imports; this is in the safety checklist.

prompt: Just check src/utils/format.ts — anything unused in there?
rubric: Uses the per-file path: `graph-it check src/utils/format.ts` or `find_unused_symbols --filePath=<abs>`
Uses an absolute path for the `graph-it tool` variant
Also verifies the file itself is referenced with `find_referencing_files --targetPath=<abs>`
Keeps the answer scoped to the requested file
anti_patterns: Expands to a full workspace deletion plan the user did not ask for
gold_notes: A file whose symbols look internally used can still be a ghost file.

prompt: NestJS services are showing up as unused in the report. Is that real?
context: Repo root: /work/api, NestJS project using @Injectable() and @Controller() decorators with DI resolution at runtime.
rubric: Explains that decorator-based DI resolves at runtime and is invisible to static analysis
Recommends excluding framework entry files and decorated providers from the scan
Classifies the flagged services as 'do not delete — flag only'
Suggests verifying with the framework's own module registration before touching anything
anti_patterns: Confirms the services are dead because the caller count is 0
Recommends deleting decorators to make the analysis cleaner
gold_notes: Framework magic is an explicit limitation of the skill.
